title: Monday, online
venue: Arthur's site (newspaper cadence: six dailies + a Sunday)
logline: The strip goes online. It announces nothing. The reader of the book sees the grid change: six a week now, and color coming.

panels.composition: Wood's bedroom. A scanner, new, beige, on the floor because there's no room. A beige computer. WOOD feeding a strip into the scanner. BARNABY watching the light.

characters.pose: feeding a page into a scanner

image.prompt: a young man kneeling to feed a comic strip into a beige flatbed scanner on a bedroom floor beside a bulky computer, a small dog watching the scanner's light, brush-pen ink with muddy digital flat colors

panels.composition: The CRT. The strip appearing line by line. Grainier than the xerox.

image.prompt: close-up of a CRT monitor with a scanned comic strip appearing line by line, early-2000s interface chrome around it

panels.composition: Wood typing. A page with a title bar: DRIFT WOOD — daily. A counter at the bottom: 3 visitors.
props: monitor: a bare webpage with a hit counter

balloons.text: Six a week. Sunday's the big one. Like a newspaper. Like the ones I grew up on.

image.prompt: a young man typing at a bulky computer, the screen showing a bare early web page with a comic strip and a visitor counter reading a single digit

panels.composition: The dog asleep on the scanner lid. The monitor glow. Wood already drawing tomorrow's. The panels have a faint, wrong, digital gray fill for the first time.

image.prompt: a small dog asleep on a closed flatbed scanner in monitor glow while a young man draws at his table, the panel filled with a faint muddy digital gray for the first time, no words
image.notes: The first digital fill. Make it slightly wrong.

art.line: brush-pen scanned; muddy early-digital flats begin
art.palette: limited, muddy; Sundays in over-wet watercolor

notes: Run 3 begins. No announcement. The counter says 3.
